claims.source_name: Japan Fire and Disaster Management Agency (FDMA)
claims.text: FDMA situation report No. 10 (16 August 2026, 10:00 JST, on the Chiba heavy rain disaster): Level 5 Heavy Rain Emergency Warnings were issued in stages for Chiba City and numerous surrounding municipalities between 19:30 on 13 August and 00:30 on 14 August, alongside Level 5 Landslide-Disaster Emergency Warnings for Chiba City, Ichihara, Mobara and Oamishirasato, Togane and Yachimata; by 05:15 on 14 August all Level 5 special warnings had been switched to Level 4 warnings. Chiba Prefecture's disaster response headquarters was established at 19:30 on 13 August, and FDMA established its own second-tier emergency disaster response headquarters the same evening.

claims.source_name: Japan Fire and Disaster Management Agency (FDMA)
claims.text: FDMA situation report No. 10 (16 August 2026, 10:00 JST) reports Chiba Prefecture's cumulative human and housing damage as: 8 deaths (of which 1 disaster-related), 3 missing, 35 injured in total; and 1,160 damaged housing units, comprising 1 total collapse, 23 half collapse, 597 flooded above floor level, 490 flooded below floor level and 49 partially damaged. The deaths are broken down as 3 in Chiba City, 1 in Ichikawa, 2 in Sakura, 1 in Yachiyo and 1 in Isumi. The report also states that all evacuation instructions that had been issued have been lifted ('発令されていた避難指示は全て解除').

description: Record-breaking heavy rain struck Chiba Prefecture, Japan, from 13 August 2026, prompting Japan's highest-level Level 5 heavy rain and landslide-disaster special warnings for Chiba City and surrounding municipalities between 19:30 on 13 August and 00:30 on 14 August; prefectural and national disaster response headquarters were established the same evening. Per the Fire and Disaster Management Agency's situation report No. 10 (16 August 2026, 10:00 JST), the disaster left 8 dead (1 of them disaster-related), 3 missing and 35 injured in Chiba Prefecture, and damaged 1,160 housing units (1 total collapse, 23 half collapse, 597 flooded above floor level, 490 flooded below floor level, 49 partially damaged). All Level 5 special warnings were downgraded to Level 4 by 05:15 on 14 August, and all evacuation instructions have since been lifted; the acute hazard phase has passed.

impact.summary: FDMA's situation report No. 10 (16 August 2026, 10:00 JST) records 8 deaths (1 disaster-related), 3 missing and 35 injured in Chiba Prefecture — the deaths in Chiba City (3), Ichikawa (1), Sakura (2), Yachiyo (1) and Isumi (1) — plus 1,160 damaged housing units (1 total collapse, 23 half collapse, 597 flooded above floor level, 490 flooded below floor level, 49 partially damaged). All Level 5 special warnings issued on 13-14 August were downgraded to Level 4 by 05:15 on 14 August, and all evacuation instructions have been lifted.

location.region: Chiba Prefecture (with lesser impacts in neighbouring Ibaraki Prefecture)
